markers.reading: Ariel tells her bedtime lullaby to Bud and Butt in Neo-Tollen.

evidence.quote: And tonight, she tells a very quick bedtime story.
Everybody falls asleep peacefully

time.basis: The player calls the scene a bedtime story and places it tonight.

markers.reading: Lyndria tells her story for elves while they are in the Dreaming.

evidence.quote: as the elves are in the dreaming.
And today, her story begins
the completion of your cozy bedtime story

time.basis: The player describes storytelling for sleeping elves and the DM frames the openings as bedtime stories.

markers.reading: Merrin tells his daughter a story on the night before her wedding.

evidence.quote: Clearly, there's a wedding tomorrow of some kind.
on the night before his daughter leaves him to get married

time.basis: Merrin describes it as the night before his daughter leaves to get married.

markers.reading: Tevren spends his one night at home with his family before his expected return to orbit.

evidence.quote: he only has a night at home before he is going back up
But tonight, I get to tell you a story in real life.
that's where I'm going tomorrow

time.basis: Tevren calls the scene tonight and says he plans to leave tomorrow.

markers.reading: Wasbeer tells a story to his kits tucked into bed.

evidence.quote: 5 little baby raccoons are all lined up next to each other
the completion of your cozy bedtime story

time.basis: The kits are tucked into bed and the DM describes the preceding stories as bedtime stories.

markers.reading: Each character is displaced immediately after their own bedtime story. This brings the five separate opening scenes into a shared sequence.

evidence.quote: immediately following the f- the completion of your cozy bedtime story
back in your body

markers.reading: The second-floor room appears to be in evening when the five characters come to on the floor.

evidence.quote: back in your body, lying on the floor
It appears to be… the evening, looking out a window.

time.basis: The DM describes the view from the room as apparent evening.

markers.reading: The five characters reopen their eyes on the Forest path seemingly a moment after closing them at Frankar’s instruction.

evidence.quote: I need each of you to just, hold hands
close your eyes
seemingly a moment later

markers.reading: Merrin’s bluebird goes out to scout and returns to his shoulder after about a minute or two.

evidence.quote: it flies off for a minute or two
The bluebird returns and flies over to Merrin's shoulder.

duration.basis: The DM says a minute or two and subsequently narrates the return.

markers.reading: At the castle Buddy expects night to be a while off. Daylight is still visible through the damaged closet when the party investigates.

evidence.quote: How long is it till nighttime?
Long. I'm not really good with numbers and times and stuff.
third snack… probably… probably a while
daylight shining through it

time.basis: Buddy places night later using snack breaks, and the DM narrates daylight at the closet.

markers.note: Buddy’s snack count does not provide elapsed minutes, a civil watch, or synchronization with the earlier room.

markers.reading: The potion ritual abruptly takes the group from the factory to the planet of the Mookers. The destination’s local time remains open.

evidence.quote: you vanish from the world that you're in
In the vestibule of the potion factory, and reappear.
On the planet of the Mookers.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: The manifest supplies no in-world dates. The transcript supplies separate local bedtime scenes, an apparent evening in Frankar’s room, daylight in Forest, and no civil calendar anchor.
yamlCheck.explanation: The episode moves among worlds with no established common clock. The spoken times for the wedding, space voyage, star recording, and closet damage refer to local plans or prior events.
